newsitem.title: USA: Governance conditions seen unlikely for IMF loans.
newsitem.headline: Governance conditions seen unlikely for IMF loans.

text.p: Concern about "good governance" in countries borrowing from the International Monetary Fund is unlikely to be translated into new conditions for IMF loans, international monetary sources said on Tuesday.
The sources, who declined to be identified, said it would be hard to link IMF credits to improvements in the way a country was governed.

"This is something the IMF is worried about, but it should not be interpreted as a new type of conditionality," one source said. "They are not in a position to put conditionality on the judicial system or on congress. It is beyond their capacity or legal mandate."

The IMF usually makes its funding conditional on relatively easy-to-measure targets such as inflation and public spending, although officials have stressed the need for good government as part of a "second generation" of structural reform.
This could include efforts to eliminate corruption or to strengthen private property rights.

The New York Times said on Tuesday that the IMF planned to make a credit line to Argentina conditional on evidence of "good governance" and it said the arrangement could serve as a model for other countries.

But the monetary sources said it would be hard to quantify possible improvements in the government of a country seeking to borrow from the IMF. "It is a concern and it is a framework for action, but it is not conditionality," one said.
